findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. Someone landing on the Athena site gets the basics in four sentences.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The title names firstmate, a project a newcomer has likely never heard of, and does not say what Athena is. A visitor to the Athena site may think they are on the wrong page until they read the lede.
findings.source:
/

Athena explains how firstmate handles work

findings.text: The page explains why it exists: the firstmate study is a demonstration of Athena. That gives a newcomer a reason to keep reading, but nothing ties the study back to Athena's main job of turning a short request into a commit.
findings.source: A study is Athena's written reading of another software project ... to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim

findings.text: What to do next is easy to find. The header links straight to it, and the section lists prerequisites, the clone command, ./setup.sh and a sample command, athena ask "add a changelog".
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself (header) and the Next steps section

findings.text: The page doesn't say which repository Athena runs on (for example, the current directory) or what the newcomer gets back. A first-time user may not know where to run the command.
findings.source: press Enter to run it on your repository.

findings.text: This header link is meant for the site's owner. A newcomer doesn't know what proposals these are or whether the link is for them, so it is a distraction near the top.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: The 'Start here' section soon turns to exit codes, locks and capacity counters. Most of the page is a detailed state machine of firstmate, which suits a firstmate user more than someone who came to learn about Athena.
findings.source: Start here: "If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued."

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is not defined. This is honest, but it leaves the newcomer with words they still cannot understand.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a durable record." (also endpoint, heartbeat, wake, captain call)

findings.text: This section and the f3 note ('A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths') are about how the page was made. They mean little to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The claim ids link to exact file lines at a pinned commit. This shows Athena's traceability promise in action, which a newcomer can check for themselves.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.
